releases.name: reeve 0.2.10
releases.body:
**Bare model names route to the pool instead of the paid default chain.** The
engine addresses models by bare id (`glm-5.3-flash-free`, no `provider/`
prefix) whenever its provider baseURL is overridden — and GATE's bare-name
fallthrough sent those requests to `default_chain`, silently serving them from
a **paid** candidate (observed live 2026-10-27: `glm-5.3-flash-free` landed on
zhipu). Now a bare name that matches a discovered free-pool model is routed as
an explicit direct (passthrough) target. Chain names and `chain_for_model`
keep their precedence; unknown bare names still fall to the default chain.

**Free-pool ordering matches reality.** `prefer` now leads with the two
openrouter candidates that actually hold quota through GATE (`nvidia/
nemotron-3.5-super-vl:free` 1M-context vision, `dots-studio/dots-3-note-
preview:free`), with the zen pair (`glm-5.3-flash-free`, `mimo-v2.6-flash-
free`) following; `opencode/deepseek-v4.1-flash-free` is denied by default —
it returned 429 on every attempt observed, including on days when its zen
siblings served 87% of traffic.

Diagnostic note from the same investigation: synthetic probes against
`opencode.ai/zen/v1` always answer 429 with `FreeUsageLimitError` regardless
of credentials or headers — that endpoint is not the one GATE uses
(`opencode.ai/inference/openai/v1`). Never judge pool health from probes;
judge from real-traffic ledger rows.

releases.name: reeve 0.2.9
releases.body:
**First-byte failover for streaming.** Live incident on 2026-10-26: zhipuai
answered `HTTP 200`, opened the SSE stream, then went silent — zero bytes for
~45s and counting. The 0.2.8 stream guard can only cool the model *after*
`finish`: response headers are already committed, so the turn is unsavable and
every concurrent subagent dies with it. The streaming branch is now a
**single-consumer pump** (one `for await` is the only reader — the previous
attempt at this deadlocked by mixing `pipe` with manual reads, and was
reverted):

- **Headers are not committed until the first byte arrives.** Before that
  point the chain can still move: a stalled or reset upstream is recorded as
  `error/stalled` (or `stream error`) in the ledger, cooled in the session and
  free-lane accounts, and the next candidate serves the request.
- **Real timers on silence, never on total duration.** `stream_first_byte_ms`
  (default 45s) guards the wait for the first byte; after that the window
  widens to `stream_idle_ms` (default 120s). A reasoning model that keeps
  producing is never touched — only silence is. A timer firing mid-stream
  aborts the upstream and truncates the response (headers are already out;
  nothing else is possible), recording exactly one failure — the `finish`
  empty-probe yields via the settled flag, so accounts are never
  double-booked. Client disconnects before the first byte clean up silently
  and are **not** charged to the provider.
- Two latent 0.2.8 defects fixed en route: the `pipe` never forwarded upstream
  errors (a stream reset before the first chunk left the client hanging — now
  it fails over), and the probe decoded chunks with `chunk.toString('utf8')`,
  which degrades to comma-separated decimal garbage on runtimes where
  `Readable.fromWeb` yields bare `Uint8Array` (every real stream would have
  been judged empty); decoding now goes through `TextDecoder`.
- Policy keys: `stream_first_byte_ms` / `stream_idle_ms` (exposed in
  `/gate/version` and the snapshot); the never-wired `first_prompt_watchdog_ms`
  default was removed.

releases.name: reeve 0.2.8
releases.body:
**Empty-response guard.** Some free models answer `HTTP 200` with no content —
observed live on 2026-10-26: a `nemotron:free` 200-with-empty-body made the
engine record an empty assistant message and go idle, killing the turn in
place (and, because the half-finished tool pairing stayed in the message list,
poisoning later turns with `Messages with role 'tool' must be a response to a
preceding message with 'tool_calls'` errors). Two layers now:

- **Non-stream responses** (`content-type` is not `text/event-stream`): the
  body is checked for real-content evidence (non-empty
  `content`/`reasoning`/`tool_calls`) before it is forwarded. Empty → recorded
  as `error/empty` in the ledger and the chain moves to the next candidate —
  the request survives.
- **Streaming responses**: forwarding is untouched (still pipe, zero
  buffering). At `finish`, the forwarded bytes are scanned; a response with no
  real content counts as a free-pool failure → escalating cooldown (0.2.7)
  keeps the model out of the next requests. The turn itself is already spent —
  the guard is that every subsequent request skips the model. The success
  bookkeeping for free-pool candidates also moved to `finish`, so a
  post-hoc-empty response is no longer wiped out by a premature `noteAttempt(true)`
  (that ordering bug made the guard ineffective: every failure count was
  immediately reset).

Plugin-only release — panel untouched.

releases.name: reeve 0.2.7
releases.body:
**Free-pool cooldowns now escalate instead of resetting.** A free model that
keeps failing used to re-enter a fixed 600 s cooldown and — worse — when a
cooldown expired the whole record was deleted, handing the model a fresh
failure budget. A persistently rate-limited upstream (429 all day) therefore
burned 3 doomed attempts every ~10 minutes, forever (observed: two dead models
burned 12 attempts in 40 minutes). Now each model's consecutive-offense count
is remembered when a cooldown expires (the entry stays, `fails` resets, one
probe attempt is allowed); failing again re-enters cooldown at
`failure_cooldown_seconds × 2^(offenses−1)`, capped by the new
`free.cooldown_cap_seconds` (default 86400). One successful attempt clears the
record entirely, so a recovered upstream returns to the base cooldown. The
`/gate/free` runtime snapshot reports `offenses` per cooling ref so the panel
can show "how many times has this model re-entered cooldown". Config gains
`free.cooldown_cap_seconds` (60–604800); everything else is unchanged.
Plugin-only release — the panel extension is untouched.

releases.name: reeve 0.2.6
releases.body:
**Tier metadata now follows the chain — no manual upkeep.** The composer's
model popover used to show dashes for cost and release date, and (worse) a
fabricated `1M` context on `reeve/free`. GATE now exposes
`GET /gate/model-meta`: per-tier cost (input/output/cache read+write),
context/output limits, and release date, computed from the **first target of
the chain each tier maps to** — so editing a chain in the panel updates the
popover data too (GATE hot-reloads; the plugin refreshes on its existing
state poll and calls `provider.reload()` when the data changes, on engines
that expose it — older engines degrade to "next rebuild/restart"). The data
source is the models.dev payload GATE already fetches (6h TTL, zero new
outbound traffic); provider names are resolved through three levels
(exact key → `canonical_model_id` → globally unique model id). Anything the
catalog does not know is **omitted entirely** rather than guessed — the free
pool's popular models have no entries today, so `reeve/free` cost is $0 (free
by definition) with context falling back to the new `free.context_floor`
(default 131072), which stops the engine from letting sessions grow past what
the pool can actually serve. `buildTierModel` ships the same numbers as
cold-start fallback (`STATIC_TIER_META`); values written by hand under
`providers.reeve.models.*` in opencode.jsonc are never touched.
